This is one of those games that has many polarizing opinions on it.  Don't let the Steam reviews misguide you.  There are plently of people within the gaming community that either hate this game or believe it to be extremely over-rated.  However, I admit, that the only reason I purchased this game, was because of the overwhelming amount of praise gamers had given it within the Steam reviews.  I saw many who claimed that it was just as good or even better than a TellTale story.
Like any other person, I love a gripping narrative.  My discovery about this game happened during a winter break; and it was around this time when I was itching for a good (NEW) story.  So I did an impulse buy, and went into the game with some optimism and hope.  Although I don't want to sound silly, I would be denying my true feelings if I didn't say that this episodic adventure has become one of my favorite games of all time.
STORY BACKGROUND:
Life is Strange is a coming of age story that takes place around a fictional town called Arcadia Bay, which rests on the Oregon Coast.  The main character, Max Caulfield, is an aspiring photography student who decides to leave Seattle, and go back to her hometown (Arcadia Bay), so she can attend Blackwell Academy for her final year of high school.  The narrative is centered around Max's personal discovery of what it truly means to be an adult.  Actions have consequences and life can be unfair.  Sometimes things just don't work out the way you want them to.
STORY OPINION:
Personally, I feel that Dontnod nailed the execution of the story.  It makes the player feel like they've known Max, for the entirety of their lives.  All of the characters fir these stereotypical personalities that fit the roles one would expect in a high school story.  But, I think that this played to the game's advantage rather than its downfall.  Being a teenager myself, I developed strong sympathy for the main character, and was eager to watch her journey unfold.
VOICE ACTING:
The voice acting in this game was phenomenal.  Every character had a distinct feel and tone.  Hannah Telle did a wonderful job with Max's character.  She perfectly captured the timid/geeky persona that the story needed.  Ashley Burch did a great job as Chloe.  Her flawless performance captured the cynical teenage character who was sometimes ♥♥♥♥♥y, but also endearing.  Burch continues to show her great voice acting talent within this game.
GAMEPLAY:
The gameplay is a simple third person linear experience, and that's ok.  It should be apparent to the player that this is not a GAMEPLAY-HEAVY video game.  It's a STORY-HEAVY video game.  Gameplay is centered around the inspection of objects, and Max's ability to rewind time.  There will be many scenarios that can occur based on the chosen dialogue or decisions made in a conversation.  If the player doesn't like a certain outcome, Max can rewind time and take on the conversation/scenaio from a different approach.  However, there are CERTAIN choices which are PERMANENT.  I'd like to note that there are subtle touches within the in-game experience, which make small contributions to the overall story.  Max's animations really portray her as a shy person.  She will sometimes rub the back of her neck, or hold one of her arms with the other.  (Lip syncing needs major improvement though).
GRAPHICS/ART DESIGN:
The graphics are not the best, but that's because of the unique art design.  The game almost has this cartoony yet realistic feel, that perfectly complements the mood and tone of the story.  From the radiant sunsets, to the blowing of leaves in the wind and rain, and to the darkness of the night, it was all very pleasant for the eyes.  It's deceptively beautiful.
SOUND DESIGN/OST:
The atmosphere to this game was so ♥♥♥♥ING good to experiece.  And I think this should really be accredited to the composer (Jonathan Morali) for the sountrack, and the director (Frederic Devanlay) for the sound design.  The music worked right along side the graphical style and changed the tone from calm to dreary to excitement and to sadness.  Songs from outside artists are used within the game, and I thought they were integrated appropriately.  This game has some of the best ambience I've ever experienced.  The simple yet brilliant "moments of calm," are perfect examples.  This is where Max can sit down and take in the environment around her, as the player listens to her internal thoughts.
VERDICT:
This is a very bold statement, and I know many people will think I'm crazy, but Max Caulfield is one of my favorite characters in all of gaming.  I love this game and I think I always will.  I have no shame in it.  I know a lot of people hate it, I know a lot of people hate the ending, and I know a lot of people think its over-rated.  And that's completely fine, because I view this game as an experience.  There will never be an experience that can satisfy or connect with everyone.  I'm just glad to say that I was able to connect with this game, and I am grateful that it came into my life when I needed a really good story.
"Time to change time..."
-Max Caulfield

What do the following have in common?
1) Surviving from 1939 to 1945 in Silent Hunter 3
2) Toyota GT1 Monte Carlo super licence in Gran turismo 3
3) Beating Ornstien and Smough on the first try in Dark Souls
4) First manned return science mission to Moho
Answer. They have all been, at one time or another my crowning achievement in computer gaming. Something that required dedication, commitment and detailed knowledge of the game and its systems.
Designing and building the rocket and executing that mission took longer than some entire games I’ve completed before now. 70% of the rockets mass was used just getting into orbit. Then you’ve got to reach a tiny speck on an inclined orbit a tremendous distance away. That’s the easy part. Then you have to come to almost a complete stop around that speck even though Kerbol's gravity has been speeding you up the whole journey. On 30% fuel. Then you must land, do science, take off and get your Kerbal back home alive. One mistake in that design, one botched maneuverer or separation or dodgy landing or miscalculation as to how much fuel you need and your valiant Kerbal is lost forever.
Are you up to the challenge?

I really enjoy this game. This series has been around for around 30 or so years and are still able to come up with new and enjoyable ways to keep the boardgame-esque strategy interesting. This is alos the first game that I have ever pre-ordered.
Pros:
-The graphics are very nice, in my opinion. I have heard from other people that they did not like that it resembled a mobile game, but they are a nice styalized graphic.
-The music is tremendous. As in the previous titles, each civ has it's own theme, but it evolves throughout each era of the game; starting out as a few ethnic instruments in the pre and classic ages, al the way to orchestras and synth beats for the modern and atomic eras. The American theme is one of my favorites to listen to as I play.
-They carry over many features from Civ V, like the hex based tiles and no two units of the same category can occupy the same tile; all of this adds an angle of strategy.
-Districts are really cool, adding a personilzed manner to the cities and allowing the cities to sprawl across your territories
-Each civ leader has their own likes and dislikes, which adds a set of realism and huminizes them. Some leader liek when you alliance with city-states, other leaders like if you wage war, some don't. It's pretty cool.
-The day/night cycle is a nice touch for seeing how much of your life you will be sinking into this game.
Cons:
-Some of the UI is a little wonky. Sometimes unit icons will overlap the city bombardment icon and I don't know how to fix that or if I am the only one experiencing that.
-The AI can be a little weird at times. Almost everyone will hate eachother at all times, no matter what you do: give gold, help in a war, whatever.
Other than just a few minor problems that I have run into, nothing really too bad. I would say buy it and, uh, play until 4 am, like ME. Or buy it and play until 10 or 11 pm like a normal human beinig. Either choice sees you buying the game.

Civ 6 in its current state barely qualifies as a game. Despite two patches the AI still  is unable to compete. There are plenty of Declarations of War - but after the first two eras the AI may (or may not) send units, it may send one unit, or it may send several  that simply mill about in confusion, never attacking the city where they are deployed., waiting to be picked off by ranged units. Capturing an enemy city also is absurdly easy. The AI has no conception of how to make use of its units. Together, these make Domination absurdly easy to the point it's not worth bothering.
Many people hate the Diplomacy. If you capture a city belonging to an AI that has declared war on you - you're branded by all other civs as a warmonger - and will be denoucned for the remaineder of the game. If you declare a joint war with another civ that civ is likely to brand you a warmonger.  wouldn't even mind that - if the AI would mount a credible attack or defense but as it is, it's completely brain dead.
Religion is where the game AI seems to come awake by spamming religious units to the point your territories are overrun with missionaries, appostles etc.  One may try to compete - but with the all critical "districts"  limited by population, the AI has to be building Holy Sites in every city... at the cost of either military encampments, trading hubs, education hubs,, industrial cites, theatre districts etc - and STILL you can't compete with the AI for spamming religious units. The only solution is to declare war - since you cannot tell the other civs to stop sending religious units. That earns you the stripe of being a warmonger - which quickly will be picked up by all other civs.
I could live with the much villified UI if the game otherwise were good.

Civ VI feels like a step in the wrong direction for the series.
The UI is abyssmal. The popups spamming the UI when it's not your turn means you get a healthy dose of what other civs are building while you listen to your units die in who-knows-where. The game is not technical in info, and tries desperately to give you tooltips on hexes when you're trying to get info on production or cities.
Diplomacy is utterly worthless. There's no tangible impact of the various "stages" of diplomacy between leaders; you'll get denounced by a friend as quickly as a foe, and it doesn't seem to impact trade or warfare even slightly. Having the secondary objectives for each leader is neat, but in the end, just serves to trigger their ire nearly constantly.
Sieges are just awful. If you have a seige unit, you're taking a city nearly instantly. Without one, it's nigh impossible unless you're two tech levels higher.
I will say, though, the music in this game is just gorgeous, and the art is great.
Not done with the game, by any means. And it is a lot of fun to play. I've got a lot more time and effort (and probably money) to put into this game, but as it is, it's got a lot of issues. I have high hopes that the game will get some worthwhile tweaks to make it better, Civ V was awful until the expansion, so maybe this game will follow suit.

If you loved the first game, you'll love this one. The gameplay mehcnaics are the same, but the point of view is different. Going from being an adult man to a young girl changes completely how people interact with you and how serious your treated. It's quite the awesome perspective change.

The districts feature is a fantastic addition.  Other than that, this game is barely playable - a huge step in the wrong direction.  Problems:
1. Diplomacy is terrible!
2. The constant annioying flood of messages from AI players... often times telling nothing of substance.
3. Addition to above, all AI messages get told on some cheesey animated screen, only to have you click where the message is repeated without animation.  One screen is enough - especially for the worthless "atta boy" or "tisk tisk" messages that come up far too often.
4. Stats?  Where are the demographics?  One of the best parts of all prior civ games are the stats!  In Civ6, they seem non-existent.  Perhaps I just haven't yet found...
5. End game is worthless.  See above... no real stats or anything!  Not even a replay map???
6. Warmonger penalty is insane.  AI declares war on you, you're stuck at war because their peace terms are asinine.  You start winning, and the rest of the AI deems you a warmonger???
7. As with above, the war weariness penalty is just wrong... far too severe.  If another nation declares war on me, I expect my citizens to not get war weary when defending outselves...
8. Let's bring back some prior game features that were missed in Civ5 (trade maps, trade tech, capitulation)
9. Where are the Civs at?  It feels light.
10. The way AI plays it means if you build wonders, you'll NEVER be allied with Chinese.  If you like great people, Brazil will always hate you.
I'm sure i'm missing a ton.  I've logged a ton of hours on prior civ games... have logged 77 on this one since it came out.  Far below what I'd expect.  It's still civ, so there is that.  Absolutely love the districts features.  Other than that... it seems this game is a step in the wrong direction.  Hoping more gets fixed with updates... and glad they fixed the inability to rename cities.  For now at least, you'd be better of buying civ 5 or 4.

Been playing on and off the last couple of years, and it was one heck of a ride. Just wish more could be added.
First off, the physics are usually spot on, sometimes a glitch will happen. And rocketry building is pretty simple to grasp, but the level of creativity can extend beyond your imagination. It's not overly complex like Space Engineers, you're literally slapping fuel tanks and thrusters together, plus optional structural support if it gets too big. Should it crash and burn, learning from your mistakes is half the fun!
Only gripes with the game are the Career/ Science Modes and EVA is lacking any sort of activity...
The Career and Science modes are the main campaigns so to speak. Science mode, you must bring science equipment to various parts of the solar system and gather science points to unlock more rocket parts and technology. Career, you manage your money wisely by taking contracts, building on a budget, and also collecting science points via science equipment. None of those modes i find to be fun at all as they are overly grindy, forcing you to do meaningless tasks like flying tourist over a very specific spot and hopping from biome to biome to collect science data. It'll take hours before you can afford to do that one project you want to do. Stick to Sandbox if you want to have fun.
Also The EVA is probably the most under developed part of the game. Yes you can make rovers, but they're pointless, unless you really want to drive literally hours to the next biome for science points. You can't fix anything, you can't build, and you can't do much of anything except plant a flag (which is the best part). They do have mods that allow your kerbals to fix the ship or to attach parts, ect. But mods tend to make the game a bit unstable with the more you add, which i'll get to in a second...
So MODS! Mods are awesome, they breath new life into a game and keep it going. This game has an amazing mod community! Hundreds upon hundreds of options out there to customize your experience any way you want! It just sucks though, that such a huge community exists, and yet it's so fragmented thanks to the Devs partnering with
and making that the primary source of mods, and not the steam workshop!? Some modders wont post there and only on the forums or on other sites. You can't get player made ships there either. We do have CKAN, which is a tool to download and install with one click, but we can't expect that to be updated forever.
Look, it's a great game and all! I loved my time with it. Just wish somethings were done differently.

This is one of those games that has many polarizing opinions on it.  Don't let the Steam reviews misguide you.  There are plently of people within the gaming community that either hate this game or believe it to be extremely over-rated.  However, I admit, that the only reason I purchased this game, was because of the overwhelming amount of praise gamers had given it within the Steam reviews.  I saw many who claimed that it was just as good or even better than a TellTale story.
Like any other person, I love a gripping narrative.  My discovery about this game happened during a winter break; and it was around this time when I was itching for a good (NEW) story.  So I did an impulse buy, and went into the game with some optimism and hope.  Although I don't want to sound silly, I would be denying my true feelings if I didn't say that this episodic adventure has become one of my favorite games of all time.
STORY BACKGROUND:
Life is Strange is a coming of age story that takes place around a fictional town called Arcadia Bay, which rests on the Oregon Coast.  The main character, Max Caulfield, is an aspiring photography student who decides to leave Seattle, and go back to her hometown (Arcadia Bay), so she can attend Blackwell Academy for her final year of high school.  The narrative is centered around Max's personal discovery of what it truly means to be an adult.  Actions have consequences and life can be unfair.  Sometimes things just don't work out the way you want them to.
STORY OPINION:
Personally, I feel that Dontnod nailed the execution of the story.  It makes the player feel like they've known Max, for the entirety of their lives.  All of the characters fir these stereotypical personalities that fit the roles one would expect in a high school story.  But, I think that this played to the game's advantage rather than its downfall.  Being a teenager myself, I developed strong sympathy for the main character, and was eager to watch her journey unfold.
VOICE ACTING:
The voice acting in this game was phenomenal.  Every character had a distinct feel and tone.  Hannah Telle did a wonderful job with Max's character.  She perfectly captured the timid/geeky persona that the story needed.  Ashley Burch did a great job as Chloe.  Her flawless performance captured the cynical teenage character who was sometimes ♥♥♥♥♥y, but also endearing.  Burch continues to show her great voice acting talent within this game.
GAMEPLAY:
The gameplay is a simple third person linear experience, and that's ok.  It should be apparent to the player that this is not a GAMEPLAY-HEAVY video game.  It's a STORY-HEAVY video game.  Gameplay is centered around the inspection of objects, and Max's ability to rewind time.  There will be many scenarios that can occur based on the chosen dialogue or decisions made in a conversation.  If the player doesn't like a certain outcome, Max can rewind time and take on the conversation/scenaio from a different approach.  However, there are CERTAIN choices which are PERMANENT.  I'd like to note that there are subtle touches within the in-game experience, which make small contributions to the overall story.  Max's animations really portray her as a shy person.  She will sometimes rub the back of her neck, or hold one of her arms with the other.  (Lip syncing needs major improvement though).
GRAPHICS/ART DESIGN:
The graphics are not the best, but that's because of the unique art design.  The game almost has this cartoony yet realistic feel, that perfectly complements the mood and tone of the story.  From the radiant sunsets, to the blowing of leaves in the wind and rain, and to the darkness of the night, it was all very pleasant for the eyes.  It's deceptively beautiful.
SOUND DESIGN/OST:
The atmosphere to this game was so ♥♥♥♥ING good to experiece.  And I think this should really be accredited to the composer (Jonathan Morali) for the sountrack, and the director (Frederic Devanlay) for the sound design.  The music worked right along side the graphical style and changed the tone from calm to dreary to excitement and to sadness.  Songs from outside artists are used within the game, and I thought they were integrated appropriately.  This game has some of the best ambience I've ever experienced.  The simple yet brilliant "moments of calm," are perfect examples.  This is where Max can sit down and take in the environment around her, as the player listens to her internal thoughts.
VERDICT:
This is a very bold statement, and I know many people will think I'm crazy, but Max Caulfield is one of my favorite characters in all of gaming.  I love this game and I think I always will.  I have no shame in it.  I know a lot of people hate it, I know a lot of people hate the ending, and I know a lot of people think its over-rated.  And that's completely fine, because I view this game as an experience.  There will never be an experience that can satisfy or connect with everyone.  I'm just glad to say that I was able to connect with this game, and I am grateful that it came into my life when I needed a really good story.

Civilization VI is yet another entry in the long lasting Civilization series. Civilization VI is a strategy game within the 4X subgenre. 4X stands for:
- E
plore
- E
pand
- E
ploit
- E
terminate
These are 4 things that you will be doing in this game. You start off with a settler and a warrior unit, and then you are supposed to found your first city. You pick a location and start e
ploring. When exploring, you're looking for new places to e
pand. Land that you have claimed is e
ploitable, by constructing buildings or improvements. Finally, you will bump into other civilizations, and possibly conflict. To win, you have to e
terminate everyone else (literally or figuratively).
There are several victory possibilities:
- Time Victory
- Domination Victory
- Religious Victory
- Science Victory
- Culture Victory
This game improves upon Civilization V, yet it also lacks some features. Civilization VI features unstacked cities, and stacked units. It also now has a culture tree. These features improve the game IMO.
The AI is actually worse compared to Civ V in my opinion. Also, you either love the art style or hate it. I like it, it's easy on my eyes and things are clear to read.
While Civilization VI had some problems for a long time, it has been improved. The season pass had too little DLC and the AI was completely screwed up on launch.
However, recently Firaxis announced that they'll be giving more DLC to the season pass owners. This is a good thing. The developers have also improved the AI through several updates, but it's not perfect yet.
I recommend this as a solid entry in the Civilization series, and a good strategy game overall. If you're not sure, get Civilization V, it's still a great game and is on sale a lot and is often under 10 euros for the complete edition.

If you're a fan of story driven games and narratives that really examine the human character then this game is for you. It may have zombies, but that's just a distraction to the real threat... Human beings.
An homage to point/click adventure games minus the complex puzzles at times to maintain a flow of the story. While I will say that for a game that touts it being as every choice matters (and it does to a point) I find myself often choosing the lesser or greater of the same outcome for some characters with really no choice on how their life plays out in the grand scheme of the main story. This doesn't happen often, but when you're left with a choice of Person A getting killed by way of X or getting killed by way of Y it leaves you with a somewhat defeated feeling.
The graphical style is very similar to the comic book, which helps distinguish it from the TV show while still remaining relevant to the universe in which it exists. The animations are done very well and really help you connect with the characters emotions.
The music is both haunting and moviing. There are some repeated songs, but they are still great and help to convey the emotion to be delivered in each scene.
Voice acting is also done well, and all fits into getting you to connect with each scene.
Overall, these games are a worty buy for a casual gamer who enjoys to sit back and watch a story unfold that has snap decisions that must be made often that affect the outcome of the story direction with key characters.

This is a good game. I'm not one for long reviews and whilst this one is mostly negative, I do recommend it as a game if you've enjoyed other Civ games. Aspects such as the music, combat, religious and research options are fairly diverse and well thought through. Different civs have their own flavour and features which makes for interesting playing.
It does have issues though, one of the main being the AI. The AI are at times ridiculous, and it can be taken light heartedly up until a point where it starts to grate. They're difficult and sometimes virtually impossible to please and ally up with, because most sorts of war will tarnish your reputation permanently. Even friendly civs can suddenly decide to declare war and try to wipe you out, then denounce you for conquering their cities as a result. Interaction with other civilisations is poor and limited, which only makes the issue of the AI worse. There are ways of appealing to certain civs, and learning how to do so is essential when the alternative is bad relations with everybody. There definitely needs to be a more complex way of interacting with other civs with better thought out AI behaviours.
There are obviously other pros and cons but for me that's the main con.

As someone that has over 1,000 hours in Civ V, I feel that I should write a review about this game after playing it for over 60 hours already. This game is fun and has a lot to offer that is new entirely to the Civilization games, at least recently, and also has new ways of playing the game which I will get back to in a moment. It also has a lot of question and sometimes bad game design and functionalities. So I will list out a list of specific accomplishments and faults of the game right now.
-Promotion system is awesome!
Pros:
-Districts are awesome. They provide replayability to all of the civilizations as you can play through each of them a multitude of different ways
-Religion is now a way of achieveing victory. This is a great addition becuase it give a purpose to the religion system seen in Civ V. (There is a con to this however that I will address later).
-The civics tree is amazing. This adds so much flexablilty to each civ, it also adds replayablilty as you can play as communist America or facist India. It offers so much more to the game.
-This is subjective, but the art style in my opinon is superior to Civ V in the sense that it is unique and allows for more individualized detail for each civ. The attention to detail is much more substantial compared to Civ V.
-Armys and Corps are an awesome additon and makes war even more enjoyable than before with the addition of some cool animations as well.
-The fact that every playthrough will not be the same as you wil not be able to build the same wonders over and over again. This goes in line with strtegicaly placeing everything around your cities.
Cons:
-Lack of content (which I know will be reversed in the past, but it is barebones at realse).
-Barbarians give and take from the experience. I am always tempted to turn them off, but in the beginning they make the game exciting and they help with civics and technological advances. They are raging to the max and later on they give up on any logical strategical advantages and charge with their spears at your tanks. This needs to be fixed.
-Civs in this game are all warmongers. In Civ V you could play the game without going to war. In this game, it is almost impossible to do so with each civ being programed to attack one another, not caring about the penalties, and their agendas are contradictory completely. The Kongo hated me becuase I woud not spread my religion to them even though they had their own, that makes no sense. This is probably the number one thing that MUST be addressed before this game can be worth the $60 asking price.
-War is too heavily emphasised in this game as I stated before. Every victory is reliant on it.
-There are next to no luxury resources in this game. What happened to jewlery?
-City states are broken and will leave being your ally for no reason whatsoever. Even if their are no spies in the game and you have 13 envys sent to them, they will still leave. They act like bi-polar prepubecent girls that just had their first period. But, because this game relys on war, might as well take them all over.
-The science victory is egregious. If you do not have sufficent production to build anything, even with the space civics, you will not win a science victory unless you have another way of getting some great engineers. It is awful how long it take to win this way.
-Hitler is not the leader of Germany
-Poland was added to the game before Mongolia (Why?)
-Aztecs are locked
-There is no diplomacy victory. This is huge and might be the reason as to why the diplomacy is nonexsistant in this game. This needs to be added ASAP as it will add an actual passive way of achieveing victory.
-Nuclear weapons have no real apperence in this game compared to Civ V as it is substantally harder to aquire uranium than before.
-Trading is garbage in this game as Civs will ask for the dumbest trade deals I have ever witnessed.
Is this game worth the money though? It seems with everything this game achieved, it failed in an aspect of it. It is fun and there is a lot of game play to get through and it is fustrateing enjoyable. With that in mind. It is not worth how much it is. Civ V with the DLC is cheaper and is superior to this game in many aspects, most of which were in vinila Civ V. I would not buy this right now and would wait for a good sale of atleast 50% off its current price. Nuclear Gandhi would have wanted it that way.

This is a good game. I'm not one for long reviews and whilst this one is mostly negative, I do recommend it as a game if you've enjoyed other Civ games. Aspects such as the music, combat, religious and research options are fairly diverse and well thought through. Different civs have their own flavour and features which makes for interesting playing.
It does have issues though, one of the main being the AI. The AI are at times ridiculous, and it can be taken light heartedly up until a point where it starts to grate. They're difficult and sometimes virtually impossible to please and ally up with, because most sorts of war will tarnish your reputation permanently. Even friendly civs can suddenly decide to declare war and try to wipe you out, then denounce you for conquering their cities as a result. Interaction with other civilisations is poor and limited, which only makes the issue of the AI worse. There are ways of appealing to certain civs, and learning how to do so is essential when the alternative is bad relations with everybody. There definitely needs to be a more complex way of interacting with other civs with better thought out AI behaviours.
There are obviously other pros and cons but for me that's the main con.

Easy to pick up and feel useful. Whether you are useful depends on your personal skill and if you treat the control point as if it contains a person with a clipboard who wants a minute of your time.
Provides a training room (sans scary control points) so you can test out all the heroes. Useful because most are locked at the start. You fairly quickly collect gold to unlock a few of your favourites without spending an real money.
Lacking any inbuilt voice support it does have a versatile voice command system to quickly communicate with team mates important information like "Push the payload!" (VAE) or "Defend the objective" (VDG) or when you are just hanging out in the spawn your character can tell a joke (VEJ). Which is also productive.
Rounds are usually fairly quick, around 10-15 minutes depending on how quickly your team can snipe the enemy off the objective without dirting themselves with actually touching the payload.
I enjoy playing and see this as my go to casual multiplayer stress relief for a good long time. Especially if more skins like the plush Makoa are released. So friggin adorable.
But seriously guys, get on the sodding control point...

I scrolled down because i was curious to see if there were actually anyone who gave this game negative feedback... i gave up :D .
Now i know i havent played this game for too long, but i do have my fair share of knowledge and experience about the game. But since everyone have already said pretty much everything good there is to say about this game, i feel like i have to mention the bad stuff. Now ofc, im just one man (16 ... more like guy :P) so i will surely forget about something.
First off, this is a GREAT game, simple enough for newbies, and complex enough to keep you entertained for a 10 raised by 10 raised by 10 raised by 10 years or so, BUT it has its weaknesses. First off, if you think you'll be able to build a truly HUMONGOUS space station that is completely unrealistic and super awesome, then you are absolutely right, but you will do it with 2 fp/s... now this problem as i understand it has a very simple reason, part count. The problem is simple, and the solution is pretty much nonexistent without changing the core of the game too much. If you want to build something large, do it with as large puzzlebits as you can, that way, you wont have a 5 000 part count and run 2 fps while trying to dock using misaligned center of mass and no rcs (ofc not referring to my experiences :P). And, dont put more stuff on it than you really NEED, ive built so many space stations when ive gone like, ''hey, we need about 200 electric charge/second to keep this station alive, MORE SOLAR PANELS, just remember, more equals less fps. aside from the obvious performance issues, and occasional crashing for unknown reasons (probably cause im overclocking, so dont take me for granted there), i wish more of the mods were implemented into the game itself, like if they'd give you a little option to disable/enable FAR and Kerbal engineer and stuff like that. Also, there are a few bugs in the game, mostly visual: sometimes when you fast forward time too much the game fails to realize your orbit is sending you straight into a planet/moon, (this can be used to your advantage :3) and you just keep on going through them. Now i know the reason but im not gonna explain it cause this isnt game dev school or some♥♥♥♥♥♥ then there is an annoying bug that makes you unable to set your target view on your own spacecraft (if you are near a celestial body - planet or moon) (or at least i think thats what they're called :D, scott halp plzz) and a little visual bug that makes your look through the surface of the planet (its not pretty) sometimes when landing, and the well known as i like to call it ''kraken'' bug, where if you hit something in space with your kerbal in high speeds, it has a 0.00000000000001 chance to make everything kraken, and, dont put your kerbals in confined spaces, just... just dont. It also is VERY VERY loud, i mean im running the music of the game on 3% and it makes my floor vibrate (im using speakers, not headset for the most part, cause ion engines involves a lot of eating-while-gaming, and its annoying to put your headset back on all the time when you have hair like me, gets in your ears.) It also looks kinda bad, but there are mods for that (dont get me wrong, textures are great for a sandbox simulator, but the plantets... i cant live without my clouds :( ).
Im kind of a big halo but this game is now sharing its spot in the 10/10 games ive ever played. (not very many im afraid)
Oh and, if you dont know♥♥♥♥♥♥about physics, and dont ever give up, you'll love this game, in case the other reviews didnt cover that enough for ya.

As someone that has over 1,000 hours in Civ V, I feel that I should write a review about this game after playing it for over 60 hours already. This game is fun and has a lot to offer that is new entirely to the Civilization games, at least recently, and also has new ways of playing the game which I will get back to in a moment. It also has a lot of question and sometimes bad game design and functionalities. So I will list out a list of specific accomplishments and faults of the game right now.
-Promotion system is awesome!
Pros:
-Districts are awesome. They provide replayability to all of the civilizations as you can play through each of them a multitude of different ways
-Religion is now a way of achieveing victory. This is a great addition becuase it give a purpose to the religion system seen in Civ V. (There is a con to this however that I will address later).
-The civics tree is amazing. This adds so much flexablilty to each civ, it also adds replayablilty as you can play as communist America or facist India. It offers so much more to the game.
-This is subjective, but the art style in my opinon is superior to Civ V in the sense that it is unique and allows for more individualized detail for each civ. The attention to detail is much more substantial compared to Civ V.
-Armys and Corps are an awesome additon and makes war even more enjoyable than before with the addition of some cool animations as well.
-The fact that every playthrough will not be the same as you wil not be able to build the same wonders over and over again. This goes in line with strtegicaly placeing everything around your cities.
Cons:
-Lack of content (which I know will be reversed in the past, but it is barebones at realse).
-Barbarians give and take from the experience. I am always tempted to turn them off, but in the beginning they make the game exciting and they help with civics and technological advances. They are raging to the max and later on they give up on any logical strategical advantages and charge with their spears at your tanks. This needs to be fixed.
-Civs in this game are all warmongers. In Civ V you could play the game without going to war. In this game, it is almost impossible to do so with each civ being programed to attack one another, not caring about the penalties, and their agendas are contradictory completely. The Kongo hated me becuase I woud not spread my religion to them even though they had their own, that makes no sense. This is probably the number one thing that MUST be addressed before this game can be worth the $60 asking price.
-War is too heavily emphasised in this game as I stated before. Every victory is reliant on it.
-There are next to no luxury resources in this game. What happened to jewlery?
-City states are broken and will leave being your ally for no reason whatsoever. Even if their are no spies in the game and you have 13 envys sent to them, they will still leave. They act like bi-polar prepubecent girls that just had their first period. But, because this game relys on war, might as well take them all over.
-The science victory is egregious. If you do not have sufficent production to build anything, even with the space civics, you will not win a science victory unless you have another way of getting some great engineers. It is awful how long it take to win this way.
-Hitler is not the leader of Germany
-Poland was added to the game before Mongolia (Why?)
-Aztecs are locked
-There is no diplomacy victory. This is huge and might be the reason as to why the diplomacy is nonexsistant in this game. This needs to be added ASAP as it will add an actual passive way of achieveing victory.
-Nuclear weapons have no real apperence in this game compared to Civ V as it is substantally harder to aquire uranium than before.
-Trading is garbage in this game as Civs will ask for the dumbest trade deals I have ever witnessed.
Is this game worth the money though? It seems with everything this game achieved, it failed in an aspect of it. It is fun and there is a lot of game play to get through and it is fustrateing enjoyable. With that in mind. It is not worth how much it is. Civ V with the DLC is cheaper and is superior to this game in many aspects, most of which were in vinila Civ V. I would not buy this right now and would wait for a good sale of atleast 50% off its current price. Nuclear Gandhi would have wanted it that way.

Here's what people need to understand about Paladins. It's not a TF2 or Overwatch Knock off, it's a purely different game with extreme potential. Let's look at the bigger picture of this game: It's a combination of a MOBA & an FPS with just enough imagination to make it it's own thing. My first thoughts on this game were that it's just a TF2 Knock off just like Overwatch and it'll never be any bit good. But after giving it a fair shot I've found this game to be intensely fun when played with friends. There are a few pros and cons when it comes to this game, however. Lots of the characters have no been acutely balanced therefore lots of the Champions are more than overpowered. Especially people like Kinessa and Cassie, the two basic snipers. All in all, once this game is balanced out it'll be a ton of fun to actually sit down and play competitively. I'd purely give it a 7.5-8/10 simply for it's creative qualities and cartoony yet brilliant graphics. It needs to balance out it's champions and add on a few more maps. Then it'll be a thing of pure genius and beauty. Would recommend, and have recommended in the past.

So originally, I was about to review this game after somewhere between 10 and 20 hours. I would have qualified it as confusing, unfinished maybe, no fun to be had, and worst of all, I almost compared it to Minecraft. I was confused, and most of the tools were unclear to me. I felt like the game had nothing to offer.
That was months ago, maybe years even.
Since then, I've had a break from this game. I went on to other things, until a friend of mine reintroduced me to it, and taught me an actual good chunk of the basics I needed to enjoy GMod.
Now, I'm not the most proficient at making the Millenium Falcon out of props or animating anything with this game but I enjoy the hell out of it. So much content created each day, so many ways to crash your game intentionally, so many ways to break physics! And BOY are game modes fun! Role play gamemodes are nice, Guess Who is fun, Deathrun is as fun as in any other game
...
I think you get the idea. This game need time to be learned. A lot of it. And I would consider it almost essential to also get a few bazillion addons along with it to enjoy it at its best, and then you need to learn almost al about it, save maybe LUA programming, but don't quote me on that. But if you're considering a purchase of this game and you've got time to spend learning it, do buy the game. To be honest, I would even pay double its price and still think it was worth it.
Now if you excuse me, Imma gift a copy to my little brother and teach him what my friend taught me. Shoutout to
for making me rediscover this amazing source of fun.

I love Story games. Anyone who knows me can tell you that I love TellTale games, or some of the amazing story Ubisoft games such as Valiant Hearts: The Great War, but I always delayed myself on this game. I watched Let's Play's of this game, up to the end of episode four, and I wasn't impressed. But as I finished the game, I really wish there was a "Meh button" between the yes and no, but I'm gonna say that my enjoyment of the game was only near the end, so I don't recommend this game. Also, wanted to note that this is an opinion, this isn't TRUE HARDCORE GRITTY FACTS. This is just my opinion in which I believe why I don't think this game is up for you to purchase.
First of all, what the game does right, which is a good amount. First, the art design, I didn't like it at first, all looked like low Polygonal garbage, but it really grew on me and this game. It felt like a real like photo album in a few segements. It really captures the essence of photo's and the enviroment. I really enjoyed looking at the game.
Secondly. the music design for this game was also quite great. It was well cued, never annoying, and even though some of the songs weren't really my thing, I can see why people jam to the songs played.
Third, the story of this game really intrigued me as a player. It was, from a game developer standpoint, a really well thought out and good story. As a player, I really wanted to figure out why everything was happening, in which you either figured out by near the start of episode five, which is what happened with me because of a specfic reason, or you were "blinded by love" and didn't figure out what happened until it happened.
So that's some very large postives, let's talk about the inbetween. REMEBER BOYS AND GIRLS, THIS IS MY OPINION.
The time travel mechanic was always on the fence for me. I enjoyed it but I think it also killed the game. Allow me to explain by mentioning other games. You can tell (ha.) that the developer had inspiration from TellTale games, so allow me to mention "The Walking Dead". This game was a ♥♥♥♥ing roller coaster of emotions, and if you wanted to change a decision, well you couldn't. Unless you wanted to painly go through the last checkpoint, hear all the same dialogue, without skipping it, and that's what I ♥♥♥♥ing adore about story games, this is you. You are making the story within the game. Or at least you feel like you are taking an actual part within the story. With the time travel mechanic, it's so much more different. You can see every conclusion that comes out of a conversation. And this isn't bad! In fact, it's really well done in this game, because it's explained and the fact you can rewind time to go to the same person with new information is great! But I don't feel like it's a story game after this. I feel like I'm on a path, or a tour instead of exploring by myself. You can argue, BUT SYSSIN, YOU CAN'T SAY THAT BECAUSE TELLTALE GAMES ARE LINEAR TOO, and I can't agrue with that, but at least when I make a decision, it's done. No turning back. So much tension arrives from that decision you made, and if given the chance to go see the other outcome, it based on what you think is the best. Sometimes in TellTale games, the most emotional decision, such as killing your favorite characther or saving them, is the best because it tells you that you are connected to that person and the game.
Now, allow me to explain the characthers, while leaving one crucial characther who I ♥♥♥♥ing hated. I liked a lot of the characthers. I really enjoyed David Madsen, Joyce, Warren, Max (at some moments she was the most cringest son of a ♥♥♥♥♥ ever but I'll get to that later), Mr.Jefferson, even I enjoyed Nathan and Victoria. They were all characthers I wanted to befriend, or punch. I really enjoyed all the characthers that Life Is Strange offered.
Now to the nitty gritty, the negatives of Life Is Strange
First of all, the script-writing in the game was ♥♥♥♥ing terrible. It's was like a bunch of very old men circled around a table and said "So how do kids speak?". It got really cringy at multiple points. So we played the characther of Max, who always says really cringy things that make me want to vomit and convulse on the ground.
Secondly, ♥♥♥♥ing Chloe. I, throughtout the four episodes of playing this game, I hated Chloe. She never helped with anything, she always felt like more of a nuisance then an actual friend, and she is the opposite of a good person. Allow me to explain, she always blames other people for things, never understands what your plan is, she always says she's getting information from people, even though you always get nothing back and you have to do everything, and she's a boring characther. She always blames either Max, or her father, or her step-father or blalalala. She never shuts her mouth and I felt like, she made me seriously disconnect with the game. Episode three was the worst episode, because it really tries to show that "Look at Max and Chloe do things, they are such great friends!". I never ever found the connection between the characters. This reason seems so unusual, like, wow he didn't like one character so he hates the game, but the plot is ♥♥♥♥ing so focused to follow Chloe and make me feel sorry for her when I strongly didn't. And all that time bonding was just time wasted, wish i was playing something else.
I feel like Life Is Strange is something really good on paper, but excuted so wrong in the game. And all of this is my opinion, so you are probably not gonna agree with me, and that's totally fine. Because this review was my own experience and feeling with the game. Thanks for reading.

The game has its quirks and its bugs (looking at you, Catherine. I DON'T HAVE SPIES YET!), and they kept some of the key features of its older games in from the start. Most notably religion, and government are there right from the beginning. Social policies from Civ V has been replaced with Civic Policy cards that allows for more customization, potentially on the fly if you have the gold to spare in a pinch.
The only thing that keeps me hesitant is the lack of official modding tools. While we got modding tools for the last Civilization (Beyond Earth) one tool was notably absent: A map maker. While it was promised on Oct. 27th on Civ's official site I still have yet to see it in that game's SDK. It worries me that we might see them forget about the tools all together.
Patches will come to fix the quirks, and if you're impatient some modders have done what they can with their limited abilities to fix some while we wait. Obviously there will be expansions for this title, and we'll see what new concepts they can mix in with future (fingers crossed for more XCOM mixing). Just do keep an eye out for the mods available and hope we get the tools soon.

Civilization VI is a masterpiece. Never before have I ever seen a Civilization game so complete and balanced upon its initial release. The new districts scheme makes you think hard about city placement, how you want to utilize the limited tiles and adjacency bonuses in your cities (you have to strike various balances between which districts, wonders, and improvements to include and where you place them), and what you want to give priority to in your cities (e.g. science and religion or culture and commerce). Builders, acting instantly, are more valuable and more exciting – and because they only have so many uses, they must be purchased and generated throughout the duration of the game, adding a new layer of strategy to tile development. The use of traders to create roads makes trading more important and makes road-building less tedious.
The introduction of government types and policies – both connected to the expansive civics tree that advances through culture output – allows for an additional level of civilization customization (and acts as another commitment to your sought after victory condition) beyond the unique bonuses for the leader and the civilization. War has become more complex and realistic with warmonger penalties dependent on which casus belli you did (or did not) choose. There is an excellent compromise between Civilization IV’s allowance of an unlimited number of military units per tile and Civilization V’s restriction of one military unit per tile in that a few units of the same type can be made into a formation and take up a single tile. Early game rushes are now more feasible, and the importance of walls and defensive building has greatly increased (especially since now at least one such building is needed for a city to be able to attack at all).
No longer is the game merely a science rush either with religion, culture/civics, commerce, and diplomacy becoming more complex and more important. Without encouraging infinite city spam (due to a city losing population by producing settlers), there are strong incentives to expand past the four cities strategy that was so common in Civilization V – creating a more balanced expansion mechanism than was seen in Civilization V. Wonder spamming has been effectively eliminated, and wonders are now more tailored to various victory conditions. Natural wonders are now no longer overpowered individual tiles but impassable tiles that provide minor benefits to their surrounding tiles (making them more balanced and causing them to scale as the city they are next to expands and grows).
The main objection to Civilization VI, which its predecessor shares, is the rather poor strategy of the AI. Other minor objections include a lack of cooperative multiplayer, extremely powerful and aggressive barbarians (compared to Civilization V), the AI making more frequent taunts than in Civilization V, and the possibility of starting next to natural wonders. Even still, this is the best Civilization yet. I give buying it a strong recommendation.

I love Story games. Anyone who knows me can tell you that I love TellTale games, or some of the amazing story Ubisoft games such as Valiant Hearts: The Great War, but I always delayed myself on this game. I watched Let's Play's of this game, up to the end of episode four, and I wasn't impressed. But as I finished the game, I really wish there was a "Meh button" between the yes and no, but I'm gonna say that my enjoyment of the game was only near the end, so I don't recommend this game. Also, wanted to note that this is an opinion, this isn't TRUE HARDCORE GRITTY FACTS. This is just my opinion in which I believe why I don't think this game is up for you to purchase.
First of all, what the game does right, which is a good amount. First, the art design, I didn't like it at first, all looked like low Polygonal garbage, but it really grew on me and this game. It felt like a real like photo album in a few segements. It really captures the essence of photo's and the enviroment. I really enjoyed looking at the game.
Secondly. the music design for this game was also quite great. It was well cued, never annoying, and even though some of the songs weren't really my thing, I can see why people jam to the songs played.
Third, the story of this game really intrigued me as a player. It was, from a game developer standpoint, a really well thought out and good story. As a player, I really wanted to figure out why everything was happening, in which you either figured out by near the start of episode five, which is what happened with me because of a specfic reason, or you were "blinded by love" and didn't figure out what happened until it happened.
So that's some very large postives, let's talk about the inbetween. REMEBER BOYS AND GIRLS, THIS IS MY OPINION.
The time travel mechanic was always on the fence for me. I enjoyed it but I think it also killed the game. Allow me to explain by mentioning other games. You can tell (ha.) that the developer had inspiration from TellTale games, so allow me to mention "The Walking Dead". This game was a ♥♥♥♥ing roller coaster of emotions, and if you wanted to change a decision, well you couldn't. Unless you wanted to painly go through the last checkpoint, hear all the same dialogue, without skipping it, and that's what I ♥♥♥♥ing adore about story games, this is you. You are making the story within the game. Or at least you feel like you are taking an actual part within the story. With the time travel mechanic, it's so much more different. You can see every conclusion that comes out of a conversation. And this isn't bad! In fact, it's really well done in this game, because it's explained and the fact you can rewind time to go to the same person with new information is great! But I don't feel like it's a story game after this. I feel like I'm on a path, or a tour instead of exploring by myself. You can argue, BUT SYSSIN, YOU CAN'T SAY THAT BECAUSE TELLTALE GAMES ARE LINEAR TOO, and I can't agrue with that, but at least when I make a decision, it's done. No turning back. So much tension arrives from that decision you made, and if given the chance to go see the other outcome, it based on what you think is the best. Sometimes in TellTale games, the most emotional decision, such as killing your favorite characther or saving them, is the best because it tells you that you are connected to that person and the game.
Now, allow me to explain the characthers, while leaving one crucial characther who I ♥♥♥♥ing hated. I liked a lot of the characthers. I really enjoyed David Madsen, Joyce, Warren, Max (at some moments she was the most cringest son of a ♥♥♥♥♥ ever but I'll get to that later), Mr.Jefferson, even I enjoyed Nathan and Victoria. They were all characthers I wanted to befriend, or punch. I really enjoyed all the characthers that Life Is Strange offered.
Now to the nitty gritty, the negatives of Life Is Strange
First of all, the script-writing in the game was ♥♥♥♥ing terrible. It's was like a bunch of very old men circled around a table and said "So how do kids speak?". It got really cringy at multiple points. So we played the characther of Max, who always says really cringy things that make me want to vomit and convulse on the ground.
Secondly, ♥♥♥♥ing Chloe. I, throughtout the four episodes of playing this game, I hated Chloe. She never helped with anything, she always felt like more of a nuisance then an actual friend, and she is the opposite of a good person. Allow me to explain, she always blames other people for things, never understands what your plan is, she always says she's getting information from people, even though you always get nothing back and you have to do everything, and she's a boring characther. She always blames either Max, or her father, or her step-father or blalalala. She never shuts her mouth and I felt like, she made me seriously disconnect with the game. Episode three was the worst episode, because it really tries to show that "Look at Max and Chloe do things, they are such great friends!". I never ever found the connection between the characters. This reason seems so unusual, like, wow he didn't like one character so he hates the game, but the plot is ♥♥♥♥ing so focused to follow Chloe and make me feel sorry for her when I strongly didn't. And all that time bonding was just time wasted, wish i was playing something else.
I feel like Life Is Strange is something really good on paper, but excuted so wrong in the game. And all of this is my opinion, so you are probably not gonna agree with me, and that's totally fine. Because this review was my own experience and feeling with the game. Thanks for reading.

Wow, this review got a lot of traction! I'm seriously honoured to be on the top negative review of Life is Strange, because I put a lot of thought and pride in writing the review. Ahh, the long awaited sequel to the first season of The Walking Dead game.
Many friends of mine know that this game, along with Bastion fight for the first place of my all time favorite games list. No game has ever had such an effect on me like TWD has. I've been attatched to every single character in there, each with his own story and relatable features. I've cried, laughed, been mad and relieved throughout the entire game. That's something that I appreciate a lot in a game.
Whilst it's hard to judge the second season when there's only 2 episodes out, I can still put my first impression for the time being.
The game is dark. Very dark. I've played for 10 minutes and I've already encountered two incidents in which I couldn't keep a straight face. Is it a good thing? Hell yes. If a game manages to make you feel sad, or disgusted, in some parts - it has succeeded in stealing a place in your heart.
Continuing the story of Clementine, who is the main character of the game now, is something every TWD fan has been wishing for. The girl we saved and took care of is now destined in our own hands. The game is intense, and you're afraid to walk another step thinking something terrible will happen again.
Unfortunately, the game took a turn to a direction that's not necessarily bad, but just... different. Whilst the first season focused on less action and more possibilities of dialogue to choose from, people to save and take sides with, the second season does the opposite. In TWD S.1 your choices did matter. In thesecond season, it seems not to be the case. Or at least, not as much as it should.
All in all? This is a must to all season 1 fans. The story continues, and it's better than ever. The new world is brutal, especially now that you're seeing it through Clementine's eyes. It'll be hard to take, I'll give you that. But I can't wait to finish this story and see what's hidden next for The Walking Dead.

As an engineer who was quite into astronomy as a kid, I LOVE this game, and it probably couldn't have been any other way. I mean : it is about ACTUAL space travel, how awesome is that?
I'll recommend it, but there is one thing I can not stress enough :
There are basically two ways to play that game : either you build crazy rockets in sandbox mode and you see if your random construction somehow achieves orbit OR you actually try to become a good (in-game) rocket scientist and launch a planned payload to a specific destination in the solar system.
And to become such a rocket scientist
And... that's not exactly the conception of "fun" or a "game" to many people.
Just to give an idea of why you need the "school stuff" : this game expects you to know what newtons are. (And no, those are not clones of a guy who took an apple on the head XD) It expects you to count speeds in m/s rather than km/h (just as a scientist does). You must also understand the concept of relative vector speed in a 3D environment... and many other things.
The game features tutorials fortunately, but they only give the basics and you'll still have to learn most of the game by yourself.
And even though the game simplifies a few aspects from reality (like for instance oxygen and astronaut's mental state management), on what it actually simulates it is ruthless : no fuel left after a 3 hour mission (for you, in the game, years have passed)? You miss your entry into the gravity field of a planet? You didn't launch your interplanetary mission on a correct date? Well, enjoy your newborn space debris! No way out of that except loading a past save. And this feature is not available on the hardest difficulty by the way.
You might say : if you run out of fuel, it's because you messed up and you're bad, so it's normal to be punished.
True.
But this is why you pretty much need the math and the scientific expertise : to actually calculate if you have enough fuel BEFORE the mission, while taking into account a margin of error as well (because your manual-piloting manoeuvers will never be perfect).
If you're fine with it, following a tutorial will allow you to build the spaceship suited to your mission and not worry about that. But I also believe it is kinda missing the point of the game.
However, this scientific grounding and this high difficulty also come with a good side.
Which is : when your plan unfolds as planned and you actually succeed, my God is it satisfying.
I usually don't take screenshots of my games, but here when I actually managed my first moon landing, I just took so many. Because for once a game had made me feel proud. Yes, PROUD. And I have to say, it's the first time it has happened (at least to such a degree).
The Kerbal Space Programl WIKI is very well made can help a lot by providing you with already-simplified mathematic formulas, preventing you from having to demonstrate those yourself. It could help people less familiar with math and physics to achieve more with the game and actually feel proud as well.
The game also features lots of mods, and some are actually all about helping you to do all this calculus. It can replace the custom spreadsheet for those who do not wish to make one.
If you don't look at any wiki and don't use any mods, then the challenge is phenomenal, even for an actual scientist, as the game throws you out there with minimal data.
You might actually like a science and math challenge. If you think you do then buy this game. you won't regret it.
If science, math, and ruthless difficulty are not truly your thing, there is the option of playing this game as a "lego" game where you build crazy stuff and see if they work. You could actually learn a lot about science and astronomy while you do that, so it might be worth it.
I know I wouldn't enjoy playing "randomly" like that and I can't recommend it. But who knows, maybe you don't mind.
Just be aware of one thing : unless you do some science and math (or have it done for you, but is that the point?), you'll never land that miniature base on the distant moon of the planet Jool... But hey, maybe you are actually totally fine with that.

Personally, I've enjoyed this latest addition to the Civilization series, the focus on each civ's abilities and unique bonuses give the game a greater variety and emphasis on which civ the player chooses. At the same time, the bonuses of each civ are spread out so a certain civ isn't limited to a single victory type. Compared to previous civ games,  the biggest changes are in the districts/wonders and diplomacy. I like the new requirements for wonders and the fact that they take a tile, as it prevents one civ from building all the wonders in a single city, although sometimes the requirements might be a little too picky (ie The Great Zimbabwe needing to be adjacent to a cattle resource and commercial hub) and often prevent wonders from being built until much later in the game. In terms of the diplomatic game changes, I'm surprised and slightly disappointed  by the removal of diplomatic victory and world congress. I enjoyed the world congress in civ 5 and it needed some work, but it definately added to the gameplay. I enjoy the new casus belli system, and I think it could be developed further to add more reasons. An additional casus belli for claimed land and forward settling (if a couple requests to stop settling near a player in the future are ignored/denied or a promise is broken, a small casus belli could be added for any cities within 6 tiles of one your own cities) could be added to deter overly expansive ai/players.
Biggest Complaints:
The art style of the civs is chaotic ranging from decent to garbage- leaders such as gandhi recieved rediculous cartooned features, while victoria recieves atleast a somewhat realistic image, but still cartoon. I'd prefer a return to the attempts at realism in civ 4.
Diplomatic relations are next to impossible, to be friendly with a civ, you must appeal to both of their agendas and even then any little thing can set them off, and a friendship doesn't really grant you anything-in civ 5 your friends might denounce those you denounce or even declare war with you, not so in civ 6, everyone denounces eachother and declare meaningless wars.
Civ 6 is a decent game, but its not worth $50+, the price needs to be atleast halved to be worth it.

I haven't played a Civ game since Civ III, after getting tired of dumb-as-doornails AI opponents and other frustrations with the series, but I thought I'd give this one a go.
The city-building aspects of the game are clever and fun, requiring some real thought into design of your empire. And other aspects, like religion and the dual tech trees and society cards, are intriguing as well and fun to play around with.
Alas, the AI remains dumb as doornails. No amount of good design can make up for an utterly incompotent AI design - especially when other games manage a decent if unexceptional plausibility in AI opponents. Diplomacy also lags far behind contemporary design - the diplomatic model in games like EU4 is just far more interesting, plausible and enjoyable. In Civ VI it's a pointless exercise in frustration and irrelevance.
Finally, the pacing seems off - technology seems to advance way too fast for production. It often seems that you've barely produced a unit before you're off into the next age, without having had any time to do anything noteworthy in the age you were just in. The tech progress can be slowed down - but unfortunately that slows down production as well. So the relativities remain basically the same, but the game is slowed to a glacial pace.
There's a lot to love in the game design, the innovations like museums and tourists and a very interesting take on great works and great leaders. Many of the flaws above can probably be fixed in some fine tuning in patches - but I suspect the completely incompetent AI will not be fixed. It's a pity, perhaps the Civ community can come up with a bit of magic modding to create an opponent worth playing - but for now I reluctantly have to give this a thumbs down.
After all the criticism of bad AI in Civ V, one would have hoped Firaxis could have made more of an effort. I'm not getting burned again, no Civ VII for me...

Alright, this review may not be for everyone. Some people really, really liked Civ V, and I happened to be one of those people. A note: If you can, buy the complete edition of that game right now. The discount is insane and you get a lot of bang for your buck there. Anyways, if you already have Civ V and feel that you cannot depart from its mechanics and style, then don't bother buying this game. However, if you are looking to shake it up a little, then I recommend buying this game as it is definitely an interesting new take on the franchise.
It departs significantly from Civ V in both art style and gameplay.
In my opinion, the slightly more unreal nature of the game (with the changed, overemphasized features of everything and lesser amount of members in units) is displeasing. I loved the realism of Civ V, with everything from the terrain to the realistic squadrons of the units helped to make the game feel more realistic - something that I love. However, this definitely should not be the deciding factor in whether you buy the game or not. If you like more... cartoonish looking(?) art styles, then you'll really get a kick out of this game.
First of all, I think that the increased amount of interaction with City-States and the ability to deliberately sabotage Cities - and not just Empires every 15-40 turns or so - is quite an interesting feature, and helps to bring out the more strategic aspects of the game, as in Civ V all I ever did to City-States was to conquer them. Now, I am actually forced to cooperate with them to make or break my game. As well as that, the fact that Spies can be captured and return is quite... nifty. Next comes the changes to the Technology Tree. Nothing major actually happens to the Tech Tree, but the major change actually lies in the new Civics Tree (as I, and possibly the game, calls it). Now, you must balance your Technology with Culture (something I never really focused on in Civ V, maybe because it always kinda handled itself - except for in the Fall of Rome scenario) in order to progress your styles of Government and to unlock some of the Wonders for you to build. Again, this brings out more of the strategy in the game and helps to challenge you on a greater level (then again, how the hell did the Kongo reach the Information Era in the 1800s in one of my games?). Lastly is the Districts system. I think this is neat, as even though it still looks like Cities occupy one tile (speaking of which, really Firaxis?), it allows your empire to sprawl out and allows you to fill up your empty spaces with Wonders, Districts, and some other various improvements. It's more realistic in the fact that cities take room - not everything can be jam-packed into one tile.
The first is Diplomacy - while I personally have not had any trouble with it yet, as I actually bothered to read the Civ's agendas and see what they will get angry at me for, some others say that things such as Warmonger penalties still seem blatantly unfair, sometimes causing your Civ to get denounced by others while defending against an attacker and retaliating to the point where you take one of their Cities. I have not had this problem, and I'm not sure if I will encounter it later. Regardless, you guys will probably never know if I do. The second is the lack of features as of right now - you may want to wait a bit for more than TWO scenarios, around ten map types, and a lackluster number of Civs. If you can't wait, buy the Deluxe Edition if anything so you get more down the road. Additionally, the power of War - from the benefits it gets you to the ease of defending your cities from attack - seems overpowered, but I'm not too concerned about that as I mainly play Civilization for the military conquests (something that some players may see in a negative light). Finally, the UI does not look too great as of right now. Text and many bits of information are cramped together without the padding that Civ V gives to them. As well as that, some things such as being denounced and declaring war seem sloppy, as the developers simply say (Denounces You) or (Declares War) at the end of the paragraph. Come on guys, you can do better than that. As well as that, Civs have no diversity between most of theitr units as they go on, and it looks like the developers started to rush towards the end of the game. As well as that, I hope they release an update on the status of modding.
Nevertheless, I'm mostly confident that Firaxis will release some sort of patch in the future to fix at least some of these issues (like the UI). Civ V changed a lot from its look in Gods and Kings to Brave New World (well, at least the colors of the UI changed). As well as that, I think the benefits of this somewhat different game outweigh the negatives of it, and it is a game that is at least somewhat deserving of your purchase (and right now, if you're going to buy anything, buy the Deluxe Edition so you can get more of that good content in the future). Some people may not feel the same, but hey - everyone has their own opinions.

Takes a while to get used to.
Let me first say I'm glad I didn't review this game earlier.
On release day of Civ VI I had over 1000 hours of Civ V-play and my first impressions was dissapointment. The district and new wonder system were so much different from V and coming from V it took a while to understand the mechanics. When things didn't go my way in the first couple of regular games I found it boring - glad I didn't stop playing. Same with the new diplomacy system, where you can't expect to erase other civilizations and still be loved and respected but all.
The much critized diplomacy system and high warmonger penalties: Well, it's a lot like real life. After these 245 hours I've come to love it. It's hard to please the other leaders, like real life. If you in the later ages wage war and capture cities you won't be loved by the world community. Instead you need to be smarter if you're going for a "peaceful" victory option. Provoke a leader you don't like to wage war on you - then you can defend and pick his army apart. Then go raging and pillaging for good loot (way better system than before - pillage a library and you get science points, pillage a bank and you get money - it makes sense). A while later you can threaten to take one of his major cities by putting it under siege. Often the AI then want to get into peace negotiations, perhaps offering the city next to your border that annoyed you in the first place. It's just more realistic.
People saying it's impossible to do anything else than constantly waging war have simply not played the game enough. It's true you can't be friends with everyone in a game (or IRL), but you can form alliances and friendships with every civ, depending on strategy and given situation. Last game I had an game lasting alliance with England even though they were on my continent and we were competing for the same space. The diplomacy could be tweaked and made better for later updates and expansions, but it's still 100 % better than Civ V in vanilla stage.
Builders: Also something new to get used to. I had problems with these units first, didn't understand why I couln't build roads or why these guys disappeared after three improvements. But now they feel just great.
Civic/tech system: So much better than ever before - more dynamic and flexible through the ages and for every given situation. But like the other new things it took a while to get used to.
Religion: While the religion system is interesting and better than V, I find the victory option kind of annoying. It's very easy to lose if you go for let's say domination and don't pay attention to the dominant religion when you are taking over cities. At first I was sceptical about the new graphic-style of Civ6, and its "childish" look would be one of the reasons for me not to buy it.
However, after watching and reading some reviews I decided to give it a go, and it has been a great game so far!
The tech tree has been changed, along with the civics tree. Yes, it has a more childish-boardgame look than Civ5, but it's dynamics are a lot better.
It has some flaws still, and as of yet, Firaxis hasn't patched them, which is a shame. The AI is crap, making stupid decisions even on higher difficulties. Difficulties also seem different compared to previous games, with each difficulty being harder than it used to be. (Warlord doesn't feel like Warlord anymore, but more like Prince. Prince feels like King, etc).
The barbarians are also crap, attacking almost always at the beginning of the game, forcing you to build an army early on, and not being able to focus on other fields (which is why I turn Barbarians off now).
All in all; a great game, worth its money during sale, although Firaxis has made some EA-moves on the DLC.

As a long time civ player I was really looking forward to civ 6. The design features in the run up to release looked promising. The youtubers with pre-release copies made the game look a bit too easy, but it was pre-release and only available on 'prince/average' difficulty. We thought - OK - by October the actual production release will improve - but no. Sadly the game is all front in terms of graphics and no substance in terms of strategy. This is meant to be a strategy game where you could maybe make friends/alliances with one AI over another but no - it's all but impossible to play peacefully at any higher levels and any war declaration causes 95% of the AIs to instantly denounce you. All of Firaxis resources have been spent on sales/marketing, thinking up features and probably testing the first 100 turns or so of a game - hardly any was spent on making it a playable strategy game in terms of AI. Following the winter update I tried a couple more games but no improvement - I have now deleted this game from Steam and will leave uninstalled for probably another year or more. I managed to avoid Civ BE after waiting for reviews - wish I had done the same for civ 6 - don't make the same mistake as me - save your money and/or be patient for a long time until the game matures
